clues.title: Pole: Pole marking
text: Black and yellow diagonal stripes on poles are common. You might confuse them with South Korea's, but in Taiwan, they are usually longer, extend all the way to the bottom of the pole, and have an orange tint to them.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines #2
text: Roads with outside white road lines and no middle lines at all are common.
In the absence of better clues, this type of road line can be a very good way to identify Taiwan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Roads in Taiwan generally feature double yellow middle lines with single white outer lines.
Thinner roads sometimes use single dashed yellow lines instead.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Hualien
text: This open landscape with forests of short trees surrounding a narrow grassy road can be found in Hualien in the flat parts of Guangfu and Fenglin.
This area can be distinguished due to it being commonly covered in Generation 2; however, you can find similar landscapes in Generation 3 and 4.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Green and Orchid Island
text: The islands east of Taitung, Green Island and Orchid Island, are distinct due to the more tropical climate, abundance of coconut palms, and lush cliffs. Additionally, it is common to find run-down, concrete pavement.

NOTE: While the landscape between Green Island and Orchid Island are quite similar, a good way to distinguish the two is that Green Island frequently uses yellow outer lines. Additionally, Green Island is slightly more built-up.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Taichung Plains
text: Similarly, Taichung features these open plains surrounded by low mountains that are often in the distance.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Hsinchu Hills
text: Miaoli and Hsinchu share a landscape of low rolling hills and winding roads as well as sparse farmland with vegetation that can look messy and unkempt.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Yilan Plain
text: The Yilan Plain is easily identifiable by the mountain ranges that are seen in the north, west, and south. Rice paddies are also extremely common as well as houses built right next to these fields.

NOTE: While the landscape on the surface can look quite similar to the valleys of Hualien and Taitung, unlike those two, you will almost never find mountains to the east in the plains of Yilan. Furthermore, the flat plains of Yilan are also generally more open.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Hualien Taitung Valley
text: The Hualien-Taitung Valley is a thin and long valley located on the east coast of the island passing from Hualien City at the north to Taitung City at the south. It is very recognizable as it consists of flat gentle plains surrounded by densely-forested mountains to the east and west.
NOTE: Most of the coverage on the east coast lies within this valley. There are also other valleys in central Taiwan that can look similar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Mountains
text: The central-eastern region that covers two-thirds of Taiwan consists of forested mountains. The central mountain range that runs all the way to the south of the island is made up of tall mountains and rugged valleys. At high elevations, the vegetation can look less tropical and feature temperate or even coniferous trees.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Western Plains
text: The central western plain of Taiwan mainly consists of flat to low rolling plains. It is common to find crops and other farmland in this area.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: **--- YELLOW LINES:**
Roads in Taiwan generally feature double yellow middle lines with single white outer lines.
**--- WHITE LINES:**
Roads with outside white road lines and no middle lines at all are common.
In the absence of better clues, this type of road line can be a very good way to identify Taiwan.
**--- RED LINES:**
Red outer lines that indicate no parking are common in Taiwan, especially in cities.
This is essentially unique to the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Pole Sticker
text: Poles almost always feature these black and yellow diagonal-striped markings that run all the way to the bottom.
Similar markings can be seen in South Korea.
However, the markings are much shorter and do not run all the way to the bottom.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: Taiwan uses these bollards with either two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.
You can also find these lollipop looking reflectors on guardrails, similar to the designs found in Japan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: North - Old & Disorganized Buildings
text: Old and disorganised housing units as well as tall dingy-looking apartment blocks are frequently seen in the urban areas of northern Taiwan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Taoyuan - Red Bricks
text: Taoyuan features these red brick and sometimes red tile apartment buildings.
They can also be commonly spotted in the greater Taipei area and rarely in other urban areas but are most common in Taoyuan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Kinmen - Traditional Architecture
text: You can find these small, traditional-looking houses in Kinmen.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Penghu - Cream Houses
text: White-tinged cream coloured houses are frequently seen in Penghu.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: General Architecture
text: Architecture in Taiwan varies in designs, ranging from cramped, multiple-story housing to flat, single-story houses with backyards.
Many residential buildings have a very boxy look.
A lot of walls are covered in tiles, usually white.
Sheds made out of tin are also featured, commonly painted in a light green colour.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Yilan - Multiple-Story Villas
text: In Yilan, you can find these rich multiple-story villas.
They come in all types of designs and are often gated.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Taiwan
text: Taiwan telephone numbers are 10 digits, with the first two digits indicating the area code. Area codes range from 02 to 08, increasing as you go south.
NOTE: Oftentimes the area code will be written within parentheses. Mobile numbers start with 09.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
